title: NEPA has taken light
text: Darkness. The whole street groans at once. Your phone is on 9%.

choices.text: Buy fuel for the small generator (₦4,000)
choices.result: The 'I better pass my neighbour' generator roars to life.
Mosquitoes hold a party in your honour.

title: Fuel scarcity
text: Queues stretch for kilometres. Transport fares double overnight. A man is selling fuel in jerrycans at three times the price.

choices.result: Your wallet weeps, but you move.
Free cardio, courtesy of the economy.

title: Landlord wahala
text: Your landlord sends a message: 'Due to the economy, rent is now two years upfront from next year. Thank you for your understanding.' You do not understand.

then.toast: He agrees to one year. Victory, Abuja style.

else.toast: He doesn't budge. You pay a ₦40,000 'agreement fee'.

choices.text: Pay a 'caution fee' to keep things calm (₦25,000)
choices.result: Peace has a price. It is ₦25,000.

title: Black tax
text: Your phone rings. A relative needs money: school fees for a cousin, hospital bill for an aunt, 'small thing' for a ceremony. Everyone believes you are doing well in Abuja.

choices.result: Blessings pour in over WhatsApp voice notes.
'So Abuja has changed you,' says a voice note. You listen to it twice.

title: Naira devaluation
text: Breaking news: the naira has lost a third of its value overnight. Prices in the market change between breakfast and lunch.

choices.result: You buy a bag of rice before it doubles. Smart, for once.
Your savings are now smaller and nobody even asked you.

title: Owambe invitation
text: A friend's wedding this weekend. Aso-ebi costs ₦25,000. Half of Abuja's middle class will be there.

choices.result: You dance, you eat, you leave with two job leads and a party pack.
Your regards are noted. Your absence is also noted.

title: Tunde calls
text: "Guy, I hear say you dey struggle. Take this small thing. No argue me." Tunde sends money he cannot really afford.

choices.text: Accept, and promise to pay it back
choices.result: Real friends are rarer than dollars.
"You too dey form," he laughs. But he's proud of you.

title: Slim has a 'deal'
text: Slim pulls up in a new Benz. "My guy, why you dey suffer? One client, one week, you go buy your own car. Come Lugbe."

choices.text: Tell him you'll come to Lugbe
choices.result: The address is saved in your phone. It feels heavier than it should.
He drives off laughing. You keep your peace, and your freedom.

title: Prophet Profit's new course
text: Prophet Profit is live on Instaflex: "VIP signals group, ₦100k. Last 10 slots. My students are millionaires!" (His students are mostly people he sells to.)

choices.result: The signals are a screenshot of other people's profits. The group is closed a week later.
Nothing happens. But you feel cleaner.

title: DoubleUp Global
text: Everyone at your office is talking about DoubleUp Global, an 'investment platform' paying 30% a month. Your colleague shows you his dashboard: ₦400,000 profit. It looks real.

choices.result: Your dashboard shows ₦50,000 growing every day. You check it every hour.

choices.text: Walk away. 30% a month is not real.
choices.result: Your colleague calls you 'Mr. Doubting Thomas'. For now.

title: DoubleUp Global: early payout
text: Your DoubleUp dashboard shows ₦65,000. A 'withdraw' button glows. Your colleague says withdrawing 'breaks the compound'.

effects.log: Got out of a Ponzi scheme early, with profit.

choices.result: The money lands. You are one of the lucky early ones. Somebody else will pay for it.
The number on the dashboard is beautiful. Numbers on dashboards always are.
Let it compound, they said.

title: DoubleUp Global has frozen withdrawals
text: "Dear valued investors, due to system upgrade, withdrawals are paused for 30 days." The Telegram group is now admin-only. The office is very quiet.

effects.log: Lost money when a Ponzi scheme collapsed.

choices.result: Expensive lesson. You will never forget it, at least.

title: A contact remembers you
text: Someone you met at an owambe sends a message: their company needs a quick contract done this weekend. Pay is good.

choices.result: Networking: the only investment that pays in referrals.
Rest is also productive. Sometimes.

title: Mrs. Okafor makes a call
text: "I spoke about you to a friend at Delta Crest Oil & Gas. Go and see them. And wear a proper tie."

effects.log: Mrs. Okafor recommended you to an oil company.

choices.result: A referral from someone who means it is worth more than a hundred CVs.

title: Police checkpoint
text: "Stop there! Where are you going? Open your phone." The officer scrolls through your messages. Your Heat is high; they have been looking for people like you.

then.toast: You talk about 'my uncle in the force'. They let you go.

choices.result: The officer's smile is very wide.

then.toast: You escape through a market, but now they know your face.

title: QuickKash collectors
text: You missed a QuickKash repayment. Mr. Felix's team has messaged everyone in your contact list: '{name} is a debtor. Tell them to pay.' Your aunt in the village forwards it to the family group.

effects.log: QuickKash shamed you to your whole contact list.

choices.result: Your boss saw it. Your pastor saw it. Your ex saw it.

title: {partner} is 'billing' you
text: "Babe, my hair don scatter. And my phone screen cracked. Just ₦{amount}, I go pay you back." (They will not pay you back.)

choices.result: Hearts and kisses emojis flood your phone.
"Ok." Just 'Ok'. With a full stop.

title: {partner} found out
text: {partner} saw the messages. No shouting. They pack a small bag, put your spare key on the table, and leave. Your mutual friends stop replying to your messages too.

title: {partner} found out
text: {partner} found out about the affair. They smiled and said nothing. That was two weeks ago. Today, it all lands at once.

title: {partner} found out
text: {partner} found out. They are outside your place. You hear glass breaking before you see them.

choices.text: Lock the door and call for help
Go out and try to calm them down

title: Something isn't right
text: A friend sends you a screenshot. {partner}, at a Maitama lounge, very close to someone who is not you. The timestamp is the night they said they were 'at a vigil'.

choices.result: You talk until 3 a.m. It's not fixed. But it's not over.
You block the number. It hurts more than you thought.

title: Two lines
text: {pregnancy_text}

title: A hard decision
text: Abortion is illegal in Nigeria except to save a woman's life, so it often happens in unsafe places. Unsafe abortion is one of the leading causes of maternal death in the country. A licensed private doctor will do it discreetly, for a lot of money. A backstreet clinic is cheap, and dangerous.

choices.text: Change your mind: keep the baby

title: Family meeting
text: Both families know about the baby. Uncles you have never met are in your parents' sitting room. One word keeps coming up: marriage. Soon.

choices.text: Agree to a quick court wedding (₦150,000)

title: Welcome to the world
text: After a long night at Garki General Hospital, your baby is here. Tiny, loud, perfect. Everything is different now.

title: Bolaji's 'small gist'
text: Bolaji, over drinks: "Don't quote me o. Daddy's friend says {asset} will move big tomorrow. Up." Nobody should know this. He does.

choices.result: Insider information is illegal in real markets. It's also how Nepo Babies get richer.

title: JollofInu is trending
text: A famous (fictional) musician tweets a jollof rice emoji. JollofInu, a meme coin, has jumped 90% in an hour. Your group chats are on fire.

choices.result: Check the Trade app. And remember: what goes up like this comes down like this.

title: JollofInu developers have vanished
text: The JollofInu website is down. The developers' accounts are deleted. 'Rug pull,' says Chirp.

title: Konnect Telecom results
text: Konnect Telecom reports record profits after a data price hike. Customers are furious. Investors are delighted.

title: Zuma Capital Bank fined
text: The (fictional) Central Bank fines Zuma Capital Bank for 'irregular forex dealings'. Its shares slide.

title: Account frozen
text: Zuma Capital Bank has put a Post No Debit restriction on your account. A credit far above your usual range was flagged by compliance. ₦{amount} is on hold. Bring your BVN and explain where the money came from at Bankers' Row in the CBD. Reviews take two days.

choices.text: Ugh. I'll go to the bank.

choices.result: Forty minutes of hold music, then: "Please visit your branch."

title: EFCC invitation
text: A letter on EFCC letterhead: you are "invited" to the Commission's headquarters in Jabi tomorrow to "shed light on some transactions". Everybody knows what an invitation means.

choices.text: Pay a 'consultant' to make it go away (₦300,000)

title: FRSC checkpoint
text: A Road Safety marshal in a yellow reflective vest flags you down. "Good afternoon. Your licence and vehicle particulars, please. Where is your fire extinguisher?"

choices.text: Show your licence and the extinguisher

else.toast: Your extinguisher has expired. Official fine: ₦3,000, with a receipt.

choices.result: The marshal pockets it and waves you through.

title: FRSC: no licence
text: "Licence, please." You don't have one. The marshal's face changes. "So you are driving on Abuja roads without a licence? Park there."

choices.result: You get a receipt and a warning: get a licence at a driving school.
Five thousand changes hands. "Next time, get licence o."

then.toast: After twenty minutes they get tired of you and let you go.

else.toast: They impound the car. Getting it back costs ₦25,000.

title: "Who you come see?"
text: A security man in a black uniform steps out of a gatehouse and blocks your way. He looks at your shoes, then your face. "Oga, who you come see for this street? I never see you before."

choices.text: Explain politely that you're just passing

then.toast: He watches you all the way to the end of the street. You're allowed to pass, this time.

else.toast: "Passing to where? Go back the way you came." He walks you to the main road, and you take the long way home.

choices.text: Drop a name: "I'm going to Bolaji's place"

effects.toast: He makes a call. A pause. "Ah, sorry sir. Go on." The gate opens.
The note disappears into his pocket. "No wahala. Walk well."

choices.text: Argue that it's a public road

then.toast: He hisses but steps aside. "Na your mouth go put you for trouble one day."

else.toast: He calls two of his colleagues. They march you out to the main road, loudly, in front of everyone.

title: Mobile police: "Stop there!"
text: A patrol van pulls up beside you. A mobile policeman leans out, rifle across his chest. "You! What are you looking for around here? Come, show me your ID."

choices.text: Show your ID and explain calmly

then.toast: He studies it for a long minute, hands it back and waves you on. "Don't let me see you here again."

else.toast: "Enter the van." They drive you out of the area and drop you at the junction. You find your way home.

choices.text: "Officer, let me find something for you" (₦5,000)

effects.toast: Five thousand, folded small. "Ehen. Move on, my friend."

then.toast: Someone films on their phone. The officer thinks better of it and drives off.

else.toast: A night at the station, a ₦15,000 'bail' and a long walk home at dawn.

title: The Capital
text: Your phone buzzes before you're properly awake. Bolaji: "My dad is hosting people at the house in Maitama. Big men, bigger money. Come through, I've put your name at the gate. Abeg don't wear slippers 😂"

choices.result: Your name is on the gate list at the Danjuma-Adeyemi mansion in Maitama. Estate security will let you through.
"Ten minutes. Just come and eat small chops," he replies. Your name is on the gate list anyway.

title: Senator Danjuma-Adeyemi
text: The Senator doesn't stand up. Rings on four fingers, agbada the colour of money. "So you're the one who knows the street. Good. I'm building Guzape Hills: two hundred luxury homes. Some villagers from Garamajiji are making noise about land that was never theirs. I need a young person they'll trust to calm things down. Community liaison. ₦250,000 a week, cash."

remember.what: You took their job at Guzape Hills
remember.say: "My liaison! How are my villagers? Calm, I hope."

choices.result: He smiles for the first time. An aide hands you an envelope and a lanyard: GUZAPE HILLS · COMMUNITY LIAISON. ₦250,000, counted. Security at Guzape will wave you through now.
"Don't think too long. Opportunity is like NEPA light: it comes, it goes." He turns back to a man in a fila who has been waiting to laugh at his jokes.

remember.what: You turned down their offer to their face
remember.say: "Ah. The principled one. Principles don't pay rent in Abuja, you know."

choices.result: The room goes quiet. Bolaji laughs too loudly. The Senator just looks at you, the way you'd look at a pothole you'll deal with later.

title: Unknown number
text: "Good morning. My name is Halima Bello, I write for Abuja Daily. You were at the Danjuma house on Saturday. Last month, bulldozers flattened Garamajiji village to make way for Guzape Hills. Forty-eight hours' notice. The elders say the compensation never came, and the workers say the concrete is mostly sand. I need someone who can get close. Can we meet at Jabi Lake Mall?"

choices.result: "Afternoons, by the suya man. I'll be the one with three phones."
Not your wahala. You block her and go about your day. The name Garamajiji sticks in your head anyway.

title: What you know
text: Twenty photos and an old man's story sit on your phone. Halima wants them. The Senator would pay a lot to make them disappear. And Bolaji… Bolaji has no idea what his father is building on top of a village.

remember.what: You gave her the Guzape Hills story
remember.say: "The Guzape story is still the most-read thing we've ever published. I owe you."

remember.what: You told the world what happened to Garamajiji
remember.say: "My grandchildren saw our village in the newspaper. Thank you, my child."

remember.what: They suspect you leaked the Guzape photos
remember.say: "I know it was you. I don't need proof. In this city, I am the proof."

remember.what: Their father's scandal came from your phone
remember.say: "You could have come to me first. You know that, right?"

news.headline: Guzape Hills: a village bulldozed, foundations 'mostly sand'
news.body: An Abuja Daily investigation by Halima Bello reveals that Garamajiji families were evicted with 48 hours' notice for Senator Danjuma-Adeyemi's luxury estate, and that photos from the site show crumbling concrete. The Senator's office calls the story 'mischief'.

effects.log: The Capital, Act One: Guzape Hills.

choices.result: The story runs the next morning. By noon it's trending. By evening, a black jeep is parked across from your house for a very long time. — End of Act One.

choices.text: Sell the photos to the Senator (₦1,500,000)

remember.what: They paid you to bury the Guzape photos
remember.say: "Discretion is a rare gift. The Senator remembers his friends… and what they know."

remember.what: You sold out the Guzape story
remember.say: "I hope the money was worth it. Those families are still sleeping in a church."

remember.what: You took their story to the Senator

news.headline: Danjuma Crest: Guzape Hills 'fully compliant'
news.body: The developer of the Guzape Hills estate says all approvals are in place and compensation was paid 'in full'. Residents of Garamajiji could not be reached for comment.

effects.log: The Capital, Act One: Guzape Hills.

choices.result: The Senator's aide counts the money twice. "The Senator appreciates discretion. He'll remember this." So will you. — End of Act One.

choices.lockedText: You're not close enough to Bolaji

remember.what: You came to them first about their father
remember.say: "You came to me first about my father. Nobody does that for me. They just want something."

remember.what: You turned their son against the Guzape deal
remember.say: "My son has started asking questions at dinner. I wonder who taught him."

remember.what: Compensation finally came, thanks to you
remember.say: "The cheque was small, but it came. They say a young person pushed for it."

news.headline: Senator promises 'fresh review' of Guzape compensation
news.body: In a surprise statement, Senator Danjuma-Adeyemi says Garamajiji families will receive 'additional support'. His son, Bolaji, was seen at the site this week.

effects.log: The Capital, Act One: Guzape Hills.

choices.result: Bolaji goes very quiet scrolling the photos. "I'll talk to him." Two days later, Garamajiji families get their first compensation cheques. Small, late, real. The concrete is still sand. — End of Act One.

title: The Senator is pleased
text: An aide calls. "The Senator says Garamajiji has gone quiet. Good work. There's more where that came from: he has a project in Lugbe, a road contract in Kubwa… He needs people who know how things work."

remember.what: You did their dirty work in Guzape
remember.say: "My most reliable young person! Come, come."

news.headline: Garamajiji villagers accept relocation package
news.body: Families displaced by the Guzape Hills estate have accepted ₦50,000 each to relocate, the developer says. 'A young liaison made it happen,' a spokesperson added.

effects.log: The Capital, Act One: Guzape Hills.

choices.result: Another envelope. You're on the inside now. — End of Act One.

choices.text: "I think I'm done with this, sir"

effects.log: The Capital, Act One: Guzape Hills.

choices.result: A long pause. "As you like." The line goes dead. You keep the money. You keep the memory of Baba Yakubu's face, too. — End of Act One.

title: Garamajiji
text: Tunde sends you a video: old men and women standing in front of a bulldozer in Guzape, holding up a hand-painted sign. GARAMAJIJI IS OUR HOME. "Did you see this? Na wa for this city."

news.headline: Garamajiji villagers protest at Guzape Hills site
news.body: Dozens of displaced residents blocked bulldozers on Tuesday. Police dispersed the crowd. The developer, linked to Senator Danjuma-Adeyemi, did not respond.

effects.log: The Capital, Act One: Guzape Hills.

choices.result: Tunde sends back a single 💔. You stayed out of it. In Abuja, that's a choice too. — End of Act One.

news.headline: Garamajiji villagers protest at Guzape Hills site
news.body: Dozens of displaced residents blocked bulldozers on Tuesday. A video of the standoff has been shared thousands of times.

effects.log: The Capital, Act One: Guzape Hills.

choices.result: Forty retweets and a lot of angry emojis. It isn't much. It isn't nothing. — End of Act One.

title: Slim's new format
text: Slim calls at midnight. "SIM swap. We clone a big man's line, the bank sends us his OTPs, we empty the account before morning. I need someone with a clean face to walk into the telecom office. ₦300k for one night."

choices.result: The telecom girl barely looks at your fake ID. By 4 a.m. the money is moving through six accounts.
"You'll still be poor when I'm in Dubai," he says, and hangs up.

choices.text: Report it to the police cybercrime desk
choices.result: The officer takes notes. Slim never calls again.

title: One plot, three buyers
text: An agent in Kuje has a plot of land with no fence and an owner abroad. "We sell it three times: three buyers, three deposits, one plot. By the time they find out, we're gone."

choices.result: Three families, three sets of 'documents', ₦500,000 for you.
"Your loss," the agent says, already calling someone else.
One of the buyers cries on the phone. The agent sends you a threatening voice note.

title: Save Baby Chioma
text: A content creator you know has an idea: a crowdfunding page for a sick child, with photos from Google. "Nigerians are generous online. We share 50/50."

then.toast: A blogger reverse-searches the photos. Your name trends for the wrong reason.

choices.result: ₦150,000 in three days. Strangers send prayers with every transfer.
"Na your choice," he says, and finds someone else.

title: The inflated invoice
text: Your oga slides a supplier invoice across the desk. ₦1.2 million for what costs ₦700,000. "Sign as the second approver. ₦200,000 is yours."

then.toast: Internal audit finds it. You and your oga are both sacked.

choices.result: Your signature is worth ₦200,000 today.
Your oga smiles a cold smile. "No problem."

then.toast: Somehow, it's you who gets 'restructured' out.

else.toast: Your oga is suspended. Colleagues look at you differently, some with respect.

choices.result: You send the email and hold your breath.

title: The magic POS
text: A man at the motor park sells a 'special' POS terminal: it reverses transfers after the customer leaves. "₦50,000. You make it back in one day."

else.toast: It's a normal POS with a sticker on it. The man's number is switched off.

choices.result: You test it on a stranger at the market.
He tries the next person.

title: Certificate verification
text: HR emails everybody: the company is verifying all degree certificates with the universities this month.

choices.result: You clear your desk before anyone asks why.

else.toast: The agent was honest. You're sacked and reported.

choices.result: You meet the agent at a hotel lobby.
You smile in every meeting and pray.

title: Room 14 calls
text: Chairman Tobi from your university hostel calls. "One big client. A widow in Texas. ₦2 million for you if you handle the chats. One month."

choices.result: You learn her late husband's name, her dog's name, her bank's name.

choices.text: Tell Tobi you're out for good
choices.result: "Old boy has changed," Tobi laughs. You have.

title: The fuel queue
text: The queue at the filling station on Airport Road is two kilometres long. A boy with jerrycans whispers: "Black market. ₦2,000 a litre. No wahala."

then.toast: The fuel was mixed with water. Your engine coughs all the way home.

choices.result: You pour it in with a funnel made from a sachet water bag.

choices.text: Join the queue and wait it out
choices.result: Six hours later you reach the pump. You now know the life stories of everyone around you.
Your legs complain. Your wallet doesn't.

title: A scarcity hustle
text: Your cousin knows a depot manager. "Buy 100 litres at pump price, sell to the queue at double. Everybody is doing it."

then.toast: Sold out in an hour. ₦62,000 back.

else.toast: Task force raids the roadside sellers. Your jerrycans are 'confiscated'.

choices.result: You stand by the road with your jerrycans like a real businessperson.
Your cousin calls you a saint. It isn't a compliment.

title: Detty December concert
text: A big Afrobeats concert at Eagle Square tonight. Regular ticket ₦20,000. VIP with table: ₦150,000.

choices.result: You scream every lyric. Your voice is gone but your soul is full.
Bottles with sparklers, people taking photos of you. Someone from a bank gives you their card.

choices.text: Watch the clips on Instaflex at home
choices.result: FOMO is a real illness.

title: Three weddings, one Saturday
text: December is wedding season. You have three invitations for the same Saturday and three aso-ebi requests at ₦15,000 each.

choices.result: Three party jollofs, three dance floors, nine new contacts and one sore back.
Strategic. The small chops were worth it alone.
Your status shows you at home. Everyone saw it.

title: Christmas at the office
text: HR sends an email: 'Season's greetings'. Then a second one: a Christmas bonus, and a hamper with a bottle of wine and a tin of cabin biscuits.

choices.text: Take it home and share with family
choices.result: ₦40,000 and a hamper. Your mum keeps the biscuit tin for sewing things.
₦40,000 richer. The cabin biscuits are gone by evening.

title: "Are you coming home for Christmas?"
text: Your aunty calls. The whole family is gathering in the village. Everyone expects you to come, and to come with something.

choices.result: Grandma prays for you for twenty minutes. You are the family's 'Abuja big man' now.
"God bless you, but we wanted to see your face."
Your aunty calls back on WhatsApp. The network was fine.

title: Iftar on the street
text: At sunset, the mallam who sells suya near the mosque spreads a mat and waves you over to break the fast with his family.

choices.result: Dates, kunu, rice and suya. You leave with a full stomach and an open invitation.
Your crate of soft drinks is the star of the mat. People remember.

title: The road is a river
text: The storm has turned the road home into brown water up to your knees. A man with a wheelbarrow offers to carry you across for ₦1,500.

choices.result: You cross like royalty. He's made ₦40,000 today. Floods are his Detty December.
Something brushes your leg. You decide not to think about it.

choices.text: Wait it out at a shop
choices.result: Two hours with strangers, a generator and a Nollywood film. The water goes down.

title: "Stomach infrastructure"
text: A party agent at the polling unit slides an envelope toward you. "₦10,000. Just vote correctly. We will be watching."

choices.text: Take it and vote for them
choices.result: You fold your conscience into your pocket with the money.

choices.text: Take it, then vote your conscience

then.toast: An agent saw how you folded your ballot. He's asking around for you.

choices.result: Shine your eye, they said. You did.

then.toast: The agent's boys aren't happy. You leave quickly.

choices.result: The INEC official writes it down. You don't expect anything to happen.

title: Empty roads
text: No cars, no okadas. Kids are playing football in the middle of the expressway. The city feels like a holiday.

choices.result: You score once and argue about offside for twenty minutes.
The quietest Abuja day of the year. You sleep like a baby.

title: Everyone's talking about it
text: Today's trending story is all over every WhatsApp group. A friend says there's money in moving fast while it trends.

choices.text: Post a hot take on Instaflex

else.toast: Twelve likes. One of them is your mum.

choices.result: You post it and refresh every two minutes.
Prices are moving. The question is which way, and for how long.
